name: Trans-Talas Highway
note: About 167 km from the Talas North Terminal on the Kazakh frontier facing Shymkent, straight across the flat lower valley to Kyzyl-Adyr (km 109), then up the valley road to Talas, where State Route 1 continues east.

name: Fergana Mountain Transit Highway (State Route 1)
note: State Route 1: Talas east up the Talas valley, up the Otmek valley (control post km 64), through the ~5 km Otmek tunnel (km 87) below the Ötmök pass, across the western Suusamyr, over the Fergana Gateway (Ala-Bel, 3,184 m, km 118), down the Chychkan valley to Toktogul (km 180), round the reservoir to Kara-Köl and the dam (km ~290), down the Naryn gorge past Iyık Janyl (km ~347) to Tash-Kömür (km 356). ISEZ corridor since the 2009 protocol.

name: Cathedral Hill road
note: Winding road (~4 km) from State Route 1 in the city across the Naryn bridge and up to Cathedral Hill.

name: Irad Temir Jolu - Chu line (Turksib)
note: Single-track 1,520 mm diesel line built as part of the Turkestan-Siberia Railway (1927-31): Nurzhan junction west across the Chu plain and around the western end of the Kyrgyz Range to the lowland junction where the Talas branch and the Kara-Buura corridor line meet. Daily Talas-Nurzhan passenger train (~7 h) uses it.

name: Irad Temir Jolu - Talas branch
note: Branch (~93 km) from the lowland junction up the Talas valley via Kyzyl-Adyr, Kara-Bulak (grain depot) and the TAEZ sidings to the Talas terminus.

name: Irad Temir Jolu - Kara-Buura corridor line (to Talas North Terminal)
name_ru: Ирад Темир Жолу - Кара-Буурынская линия (до терминала Талас-Северный)
note: Turksib section west through the Kara-Buura corridor to the Talas North Terminal on the frontier facing Shymkent, the only protocol crossing handling trains (antimony, lint, beef reefers leave here).

name: Irad Temir Jolu - Nurzhan north line
note: Line from Nurzhan past the freight depot to the rail-only border station north of the city where trains are exchanged with the Kazakh network.

name: Irad Temir Jolu - eastern corridor to Boz-Korgon
note: Rail stub (~41 km) east from Nurzhan through the eastern Chu fields to the Boz-Korgon security depot, beside the guarded road; no passenger service.

name: Irad Temir Jolu - Sary-Bulak and Chatkal spur
note: Industrial spur (~26 km) from Talas across the fans to the Kara-Suu Canyon mouth and up the gorge floor to the Sary-Bulak Antimony Works; siding repairs budgeted for the 2026-27 restart.

name: Irad Temir Jolu - Chatkal smelter siding
note: Siding (~21 km) leaving the Sary-Bulak spur near the canyon mouth, west along the foothills and up the valley to the Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex.

name: Irad Temir Jolu - TAEZ sidings
note: Short sidings to the cold-chain rail terminal of the Talas Agribusiness Export Zone west of Semiz.

name: Talas-Nurzhan road (lowland route)
note: All-season road (~334 km) out of the Talas valley via Kyzyl-Adyr, round the western end of the Kyrgyz Range and east along the main road below the range, then across the Chu plain to Nurzhan; used in winter when the Kök-Bel road is shut.

name: Kök-Bel road
note: Shorter summer route Talas-Nurzhan (~225 km) over the ~2,670 m Kök-Bel Pass (km 53) across the Kyrgyz Range, up the valley past Toguz-Bulak (snowplough depot); the pass lies in tribal pasture between the two Toguz-Bulak crossings. Paved in the territorial period; buses and trucks in summer.

name: Chu highway (Nurzhan - Chu Gate)
note: Main road-freight route (~116 km) south-east from Nurzhan across the Chu plain and east along the foot of the hills to the Chu Gate crossing into Kazakhstan; Trans-Chuy's bonded trucking corridor.

name: Boz-Korgon branch road
note: Guarded road (~35 km) east from Nurzhan beside the rail stub to the Boz-Korgon compound (UNMI patrols barred since 2023).

name: Sary-Bulak branch road
note: Road (~24 km) from Talas across the fans to the Kara-Suu Canyon mouth checkpoint and up the gorge to the Sary-Bulak works and the Chatkal smelter turn; 3 buses a day from Talas (1 h 30).

name: Chatkal smelter road
note: Road (~40 km) from Talas west along the foothills and up the next valley to the Chatkal smelter and the Kemer mine.

name: Talas - Qara-Chik checkpoint road
note: Road (~37 km) from Talas via Kalba (livestock inspection pens) and past UNMI Kara-Oi up the valley to the Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint, the main crossing; continues as a gravel track on the tribal side.

name: Kenkol Pass road
note: Graded unpaved 1960s military road (~35 km) from the western Talas valley up the Kenkol valley to the pass; crosses the line at the Kara-Bulak crossing; snowbound most of winter; mined in 1992/2007.

name: Western Karakol valley road
note: All-weather road (~20 km) from State Route 1 in the western Suusamyr east along the valley and up the Western Karakol valley to Karakol village (~2,550 m) and its logistics depot; leaves the ISEZ corridor at the Suusamyr crossing.

name: Tash-Kömür - Uzbek border road
note: Regional road continuing State Route 1 down the Naryn past Kapka-Tash and the lower cascade stations toward Uzbekistan, the start of Irad's southern road transit.

name: Nurzhan Petroleum Pipeline
note: ~90 km buried, insulated crude trunk line (mid-1950s) from the main field collection station WNW of Nurzhan along the Uzun-Kyr fields (route kept south of the Chu, inside Chu District) across the irrigated Chu District to Refinery No. 1 and the tank farm in the eastern industrial zone; guarded by the Gendarmerie and 2nd Motor Rifle Brigade.

name: Northern Export Feeder
note: 85 km, 530 mm crude line (Nov 2000; IPTC, NurGaz 51%) NE from the NurGaz tank farm across the Chu plain and semi-desert to the metering station on the eastern Kazakh frontier, into KazTransOil (toward Shymkent / Russia); two intermediate pumping stations.

name: Nurzhan - Talas Air Base products pipeline
name_ir: Talas Aba Bazasynyn kuyaar mai tütügü
note: Jet-fuel pipeline (~340 km) laid in the territorial period from the Nurzhan refinery to the fuel farm at Talas Air Base, beside the railway's lowland corridor.

name: Muyunkum gas line
note: Small gas line from Soviet-era wells on the southern margin of the Muyunkum field (supplied under a clan-council arrangement) to the Nurzhan Gas Compressor Station.

name: Chu Irrigation Canal System (main canal)
note: Trunk of the ~1,200 km lower-Chu network (1930s-70s, >80,000 ha) run by the Chu Valley Irrigation Inspectorate from Nurzhan; drawn from the headworks where the Chu enters the ISEZ, along the southern side of the river past Nurzhan to the western farms (route schematic).

name: Eski-Aryk
note: 19 km branch canal west of Nurzhan partly on the bed of the medieval canal of Shahr-i Buzurg, ending in sluices at Shaar-Döbö.

name: Jangy-Aryk
note: 25 km concrete-lined branch (1963-66, 4 m3/s, 5,000 ha) north of Nurzhan serving Shahr-i Nav.

name: Kashkar-Aryk
note: Spring-fed ~5 km stream/canal from below the Old Citadel terrace through northern Talas gardens to the river (partly culverted 1970s).

name: Toktogul northern export power line
note: High-voltage export line from the ISEZ switchyard below the dam along the State Route 1 corridor to Talas and west beside the Trans-Talas Highway to the Kazakh grid (~440 km).

name: Toktogul southern export power line
note: Export line from the switchyard down the Lower Naryn cascade past Tash-Kömür toward Uzbekistan (schematic).

name: Fergana rim road (Tash-Kömür – Bazar-Korgon)
note: Main road of the Lower Naryn farm belt, from Tash-Kömür down the Naryn and east along the northern Fergana rim through Korgoncho and Sopol-Tepa to Bazar-Korgon and the Uzbek frontier.

name: Mailuu-Suu road
note: Valley road from the farm belt up the Mailuu-Suu River to the former uranium town; crosses the line at the Mailuu-Suu road crossing.

name: Arslanbob road
note: Road from Bazar-Korgon up the Kara-Unkur valley to Arslanbob and its walnut forest; crosses the line at the Arslanbob road crossing.
